subject: Decision Making
subcategory: The Science of Risk and Reward
title: Health Risk Decisions

hook.text: Smoking kills one in two long-term users. Yet people still start.

buildup.text: Hyperbolic discounting makes us value immediate pleasure over distant consequences.

discovery.text: We accept daily risks without thinking: driving, eating processed food, sitting all day.

twist.text: We fear rare health risks like plane crashes or rare diseases but ignore common ones like obesity that kill millions.

climax.text: Good health decisions require overriding instinct. Our brains discount slow-building risks and amplify vivid rare ones.

punchline.text: Health Risk Decisions: good judgment beats certainty every time.

quiz.question: What is hyperbolic discounting?
options: Giving extra importance to future events
Overvaluing immediate rewards while undervaluing future consequences
